speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing some new movement issues alongside psychiatric concerns. Can you describe exactly what these movements look like and when they first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that context. Can you describe the specific movements you are experiencing, such as whether they involve stiffness, tremors, or restlessness? I also need to know if these movements are constant or if they come and go.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms strongly suggest akathisia, a known side effect of risperidone. Do you feel an intense internal sense of unease or anxiety that drives you to move, rather than just simple physical restlessness?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your history confirms no substance use that could explain these symptoms. Given the onset after starting risperidone and your description of inner restlessness, this is consistent with drug-induced akathisia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia
